basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 40.' and it opens '(Vers. 40.) Et fratri tuo servies: et erit quando depones, et solves jugum illius de'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 40.) Et fratri tuo servies: et erit quando depones, et solves jugum illius de collo tuo. Signat quod Idumaei servituri sint Judaeis, et tempus esse venturum, quando de collo jugum servitutis abjiciant, eorumque imperio contradicant. Secundum autem Septuaginta Interpretes, qui dixerunt: Erit autem cum deposueris, et solveris jugum de collo tuo, videtur pendere sententia, nec esse completa.
